# FAT32 image fixtures

This directory holds a real FAT32 filesystem image generated by the host
`mkfs.fat` utility.  It is committed so the driver can be exercised against
metadata produced by an independent implementation, not only by
`Fat32::format`.

| File           | Size    | Purpose                                                      |
|----------------|---------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `sample.fat32` | 64 MiB  | Empty FAT32 volume, 512-byte sectors, 1 sector/cluster        |

The image uses 512-byte clusters because FAT32 requires at least 65,525
data clusters; smaller images (for example 256 KiB) cannot be valid FAT32
volumes.  `fsck.fat -n` reports a clean filesystem.

## Regenerating

```bash
cd crates/caplet-fs/tests/fixtures
truncate -s 64M sample.fat32
mkfs.fat -F 32 -s 1 -S 512 -n CAPLET sample.fat32
fsck.fat -n sample.fat32
```

`crates/caplet-fs/tests/fat32_mkfs.rs` also creates temporary 64 MiB images
at test time when `mkfs.fat` is installed.  Tests that require host tooling
skip cleanly when it is unavailable; the committed fixture remains usable
without any host tools.
